It separates planning and response resources from science, statistics, public guidance and alerts.
The collection links the Adverse Weather and Health Plan and cold-weather awareness material.
It links guidance for supporting people who are more vulnerable before and during cold weather.
It links cold-specific evidence from the Health Effects of Climate Change report.
It links the Cold-Health Alerting system and public advice on keeping warm and well.

families.topic: impact-and-likelihood based cold-health alerts and the core winter alerting period
evidence_points: Cold-Health Alerts are issued when forecast cold could significantly affect health.
UKHSA and the Met Office jointly assess forecast conditions and likely health impacts.
The core alerting period runs from 1 November to 31 March.
Extraordinary alerts may be issued outside the core period when cold could affect health.
Alerts use yellow, amber and red levels.
The alert level reflects both expected impact and the likelihood of those impacts.
The page is an official GOV.UK source for impact-and-likelihood based cold-health alerts and the core winter alerting period and was opened successfully on 31 July 2026.

families.page_title: Cold-Health Alert action card for commissioners
evidence_points: The card is intended for health and social care commissioners, local authorities, directors of public health and Integrated Care Systems.
It covers year-round action, pre-winter readiness and yellow, amber and red alert responses.
Commissioners should coordinate local plans with NHS, resilience and local-government partners.
Preparedness includes accessible risk communication for vulnerable and underserved groups.
Plans should account for surges in demand and maintain current emergency contacts.
Commissioners should identify organisations and communities that are particularly vulnerable to cold.

evidence_points: The card is intended for hospitals, residential care, community sites and home-care services.
It covers all-year planning, pre-winter readiness and yellow, amber and red alert actions.
Providers should tailor suggested actions to their setting and local arrangements.
Cold-weather plans and business-continuity arrangements should be audited before winter.
Settings should identify people at higher risk and have clear escalation and support arrangements.
Relevant settings should be able to monitor environmental and clinical indicators where appropriate.
